newsitem.title: USA: Ford boosts stake in Turkey venture.
newsitem.headline: Ford boosts stake in Turkey venture.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Monday it will increase its investment in its Otosan Turkish automobile venture to 41 percent from 30 percent.
Under an agreement between Ford and Koc Holding AS, Ford said it will boost its stake in the venture by buying shares from Koc companies and Koc family members. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The U.S. No. 2 automaker said the deal will equalize Koc and Ford holdings and management responsibilities in Otosan. Formed in 1959, the venture produces the Ford Escort small car and Ford Cargo and Ford Transit commercial trucks in Turkey.

Ford also imports into Turkey several of its European and North American models, including the Mondeo sedan and Explorer sport/utility vehicle. Last week, Ford added its Ford Fiesta and Ford Ka small cars to Otosan's product lineup.
Koc and Ford officials said they expect to finalize the agreement this summer after review of the new articles of incorpration by Otosan's board and shareholders.
"This is a step toward a growing Ford presence in Turkey, which we believe continues to offer great potential," said Ford Vice Chairman Wayne Booker in a statement.

Reached later, Ford spokesman Tom Hoyt said the automaker paid $48 million for its additional shares in Otosan. He said individual investors own the remaining 18 percent of Otosan not owned by Ford and Koc.
